mainTopic: Non-Jewish cheese, milk, bread and oil: reasons for the bans and how far they reach
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question about רבי יהושע: one source reflects his view before he changed his mind, the other after, and a משנה is not rewritten once taught. Three אמוראים then give reasons why the Sages banned non-Jewish cheese: pig fat on the surface, vinegar used to curdle it, or sap of עורלה used to curdle it. The עורלה reason fits רבי אליעזר, and even רבי יהושע if the sap comes from the fruit. Then the גמרא asks why the vinegar and עורלה reasons do not make the cheese forbidden for benefit too, and it leaves this as a difficulty. After a short aggadah comparing a תלמיד חכם to a perfume flask, a new משנה lists non-Jewish foods that are forbidden to eat but not forbidden for benefit, such as milk, bread and oil. The גמרא explains why milk a גוי milked is a problem even though non-kosher milk can usually be detected. It then shows that bread was banned because of חתנות and was never permitted by a court, despite stories about רבי that people misunderstood. רבי חלבו and רבי יוחנן limit the leniency of a non-Jewish baker, and the story of איבו shows the ban was enforced. Finally, the גמרא turns to oil, where רב says דניאל decreed the ban; שמואל's view comes on the next amud.

steps.title: One source is from before the retraction, the other from after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction from just before. One source reflects רבי יהושע's view before he took back his reason, and the other reflects his view after. The outdated משנה was simply left in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is before the retraction, there it is after the retraction, and a משנה does not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction it raised just before this section. The two sources reflect two different stages of רבי יהושע's thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע changed his mind. One משנה records his earlier position and the other records his later one. The earlier משנה was never erased, because once a משנה is taught it stays as it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the retraction, before he took back his view
A משנה does not move from its place; once taught, its text is not changed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the older משנה is a mistake or was corrected. It was deliberately left as first taught, even though the ruling in it was later taken back.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a משנה is left as first taught helps explain other places where a משנה seems to hold a view that was later dropped.

phrases.english: Here, it is before the retraction,
phrases.notes: The 'retraction' is רבי יהושע taking back the reason he first gave.

phrases.english: there, it is after the retraction,
and a mishnah does not move from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן קוֹדֶם חֲזָרָה, כָּאן לְאַחַר חֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources by time: before and after a change of mind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to contradict each other about רבי יהושע's reasoning
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source reflects a different stage of his view, and the earlier משנה was not changed

steps.title: Reason one: they smooth the cheese with pig fat
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיא, in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה, says the cheese is forbidden because non-Jews coat its surface with pig fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מלכיא said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: Because they smooth its surface with pig fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new list of reasons for why the Sages banned non-Jewish cheese. This is the first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason has nothing to do with how the cheese is curdled. The problem is only the outside of the cheese, which is smoothed with a forbidden fat.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מַלְכִּיָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Malkiyya said in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava:
Because they smooth its surface
phrases.notes: 'It' is the non-Jews' cheese that the משנה forbids.

phrases.english: with pig fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מַלְכִּיָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new list of reasons for the ban on cheese
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheese is forbidden because its surface is smoothed with pig fat

steps.title: Reason two: they curdle it with vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the cheese is forbidden because it is curdled with vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Because they curdle it with vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reason. This time the problem is the vinegar used to make the cheese set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is inside the cheese, in what curdles it. The vinegar is a problem because it comes from non-Jews' wine, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They curdle it, make the milk set into cheese

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Because they curdle it with vinegar.
phrases.notes: The vinegar is made from non-Jews' wine, which is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different reason from the one in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheese is forbidden because it is curdled with forbidden vinegar

steps.title: Reason three: they curdle it with sap of עורלה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the cheese is forbidden because it is curdled with sap from an עורלה tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Because they curdle it with sap of עורלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives yet another reason: the curdling agent is sap from a tree in its first three years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason only works if sap counts as 'fruit' of the tree, since עורלה forbids the tree's fruit. That assumption is what the גמרא questions next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Because they curdle it with sap of orlah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reason, alongside steps 2 and 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheese is forbidden because it is curdled with sap of עורלה

steps.title: Whose view does the עורלה reason follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that sap of עורלה is forbidden, as רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask which earlier sage רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason fits. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that sap counts as fruit for עורלה. So the גמרא wants to find a תנא who supports this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? Which sage's view is this?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
phrases.notes: Asking whose view supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason from step 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the source behind step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that sap of עורלה is forbidden as fruit

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר, who says sap counts as fruit
steps.stepSummary: The reason fits רבי אליעזר, who rules that cheese curdled with sap of עורלה is forbidden because the sap counts as fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: One who curdles with sap of עורלה, it is forbidden, because it is fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a source where רבי אליעזר forbids cheese curdled with sap of עורלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats sap as the tree's 'fruit', so the עורלה rule applies to it. That is exactly what רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא (sage of the משנה period)

phrases.english: Like this Tanna, as it was taught:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who curdles with sap of orlah — it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the cheese that was curdled this way.

phrases.english: because it is fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר, who holds that sap of עורלה is forbidden as fruit

steps.title: It can even fit רבי יהושע: he agrees about fruit sap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that רבי יהושע could also agree. He argues with רבי אליעזר only about sap from the branch, not sap from the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יהושע. רבי יהושע disagrees with רבי אליעזר only about sap of the branch, but about sap of the fruit he agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא widens its answer. רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason does not have to depend only on רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר disagree only about sap that comes from the wood or branch. Everyone agrees that sap from the fruit itself is forbidden as עורלה. So if the cheese is curdled with fruit sap, both sages would forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sap of the branch or trunk

steps.whatToRemember: There are three reasons for the cheese ban: pig fat, vinegar, and sap of עורלה. The עורלה reason fits רבי אליעזר. It also fits רבי יהושע if the sap comes from the fruit, since he only argues about sap from the branch.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי יהושע allows all sap. His argument with רבי אליעזר is only about sap from the branch; he agrees that fruit sap is forbidden.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only disagrees
with Rabbi Eliezer
regarding sap of the branch,
but regarding sap of the fruit, he agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the answer of step 6 so it fits רבי יהושע as well
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע forbid sap that comes from the fruit
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason works according to both sages if the curdling sap comes from the fruit

steps.title: רבי יהושע's own words prove that sap from unripe fruit is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע in the משנה. He says sap from leaves and roots is permitted, but sap from unripe figs is forbidden because it counts as fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned: רבי יהושע said, I heard clearly that if someone curdles cheese with sap from the leaves or the roots, it is permitted. With sap from unripe figs, it is forbidden, because that sap counts as fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for what it said in Step 7. רבי יהושע himself agrees that sap coming from the fruit is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 claimed that רבי יהושע only disagrees about sap from the branch. This quote proves it: he permits sap from leaves and roots but forbids sap from unripe figs, because that sap counts as fruit. So רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason works according to רבי יהושע too.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what we learned (in a משנה), introducing support
I heard it clearly, as an explicit tradition
Fruit, which is what the laws of עורלה apply to

phrases.english: And this is what we learned:
Rabbi Yehoshua said:
I heard explicitly
that one who curdles with the sap of the leaves
and with the sap of the roots, it is permitted;
with the sap of unripe figs, it is forbidden,
because it is fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of Step 7 from רבי יהושע's own words
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהושע agrees that sap from the fruit is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the משנה, where רבי יהושע forbids sap of unripe figs because it counts as fruit

steps.title: Both reasons should make the cheese forbidden even for benefit
steps.stepSummary: Under both רב חסדא and רב נחמן בר יצחק, the cheese should be forbidden for benefit, and the גמרא leaves this as a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether you follow רב חסדא or רב נחמן בר יצחק, the cheese should be forbidden even for benefit. This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges both reasons at once and admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentile wine (and vinegar made from it) and עורלה are both forbidden for any benefit, not only for eating. If the cheese contained them, it should be forbidden for benefit as well. But according to the חכמים in the earlier משנה, the cheese is only forbidden to eat, not for benefit, so both reasons run into a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether according to this one or according to that one
It should be forbidden for benefit
A prohibition against getting any benefit, not just against eating
It is a difficulty, a question left unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: Here קשיא means 'this is a real problem we can't answer.' It is not a formal disproof that throws the opinions out completely.

phrases.english: Both according to Rav Chisda,
phrases.notes: He gave the vinegar reason in Step 3.

phrases.english: and according to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak,
it should be forbidden for benefit!
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְרַב חִסְדָּא, בֵּין לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, תִּתְּסַר בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason, the גמרא raises a problem that hits both his reason and רב חסדא's
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasons of רב חסדא (vinegar) and רב נחמן בר יצחק (עורלה sap)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ingredients are forbidden for benefit, so cheese made with them should be forbidden for benefit too, which is not how the cheese is treated

steps.title: A Torah scholar is like a flask of perfume
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בריה דרב חסדא explains ״לריח שמניך טובים״. A תלמיד חכם is like a perfume flask whose scent spreads only when it is open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן the son of רב חסדא taught: what does the פסוק ״לריח שמניך טובים״ mean? What is a Torah scholar like? Like a flask of perfume. When it is open, its scent spreads. When it is covered, its scent does not spread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the cheese discussion and begins an aggadic teaching about a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perfume only helps others when the flask is open. In the same way, a תלמיד חכם's Torah benefits people when he shares and teaches it, not when he keeps it closed up.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught or expounded a פסוק

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman son of Rav Chisda expounded:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Your ointments have a goodly fragrance"?
To what is a Torah scholar comparable?
To a flask of perfume:
when uncovered, its scent spreads;
when covered, its scent does not spread.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: aggadah on a פסוק, after the cheese discussion ended with a קשיא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם is like a perfume flask: his Torah spreads its good influence when he shares it openly

steps.title: Hidden things are revealed to the scholar
steps.stepSummary: The word עלמות is read as עלומות, meaning hidden things. Matters hidden from the תלמיד חכם become revealed to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: things hidden from him are revealed to him, as it says ״עלמות אהבוך״. Read it as עלומות, hidden things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a first extra reward for the תלמיד חכם, based on rereading a word in the next part of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Literally the פסוק says 'maidens love you.' By reading עלמות as עלומות ('hidden things'), the גמרא teaches that hidden knowledge becomes clear to the scholar who shares his Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also, introducing an added point
Maidens, the plain meaning of the word in the פסוק
Read into it, a rereading of the word for a teaching

phrases.english: And moreover,
matters that are hidden from him are revealed to him,
as it is stated: "Maidens love you";
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:3, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: read into it: "hidden things."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁמְּכוּסִּין מִמֶּנּוּ מִתְגַּלִּין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reward to the perfume teaching of Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hidden matters are revealed to the תלמיד חכם

steps.title: The Angel of Death loves the scholar
steps.stepSummary: עלמות is read as על מות, 'the one over death.' The מלאך המות loves the תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: the Angel of Death loves him, as it says ״עלמות אהבוך״. Read it as על מות, 'the one over death' loves you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reward, reading the same word a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting עלמות into two words, על מות, gives 'over death.' So the one in charge of death loves the scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: Over death, the one in charge of death

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת אוֹהֲבוֹ,
phrases.english: And moreover, the Angel of Death loves him,
as it is stated: "Maidens love you";
read into it: "over death."
phrases.notes: The one word עלמות is split into two words here: על מות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת אוֹהֲבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rereading of עלמות, adding another reward
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאך המות loves the תלמיד חכם

steps.title: The scholar inherits two worlds
steps.stepSummary: עלמות is read as עולמות, worlds. The תלמיד חכם inherits both עולם הזה and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: he inherits two worlds, this world and the World to Come, as it says עלמות. Read it as עולמות, worlds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third and final reward from the word עלמות, which closes this aggadic teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural עולמות, 'worlds,' means at least two. So the scholar gets both עולם הזה and עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: One word in the פסוק, עלמות, is read three ways: עלומות (hidden things revealed), על מות (the Angel of Death loves him), and עולמות (two worlds). All three describe the rewards of a תלמיד חכם who spreads his Torah like open perfume.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁנּוֹחֵל שְׁנֵי עוֹלָמוֹת,
phrases.english: And moreover, he inherits two worlds:
one is this world
and one is the World to Come,
as it is stated: "Maidens";
read into it: "worlds."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁנּוֹחֵל שְׁנֵי עוֹלָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final rereading of עלמות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תלמיד חכם inherits both עולם הזה and עולם הבא

steps.title: The new list opens with milk, bread and oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new list of gentile foods that are forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. It starts with milk milked by a גוי without a Jew watching, their bread and their oil, and notes that רבי and his court permitted the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: These gentile items are forbidden, but not forbidden for benefit: milk a גוי milked when no Jew saw it, their bread and their oil. רבי and his court permitted the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a fresh list of gentile foods. Unlike the earlier list, these may not be eaten, but one may still sell them or use them for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key distinction is between אסור באכילה (forbidden to eat) and אסור בהנאה (forbidden to use for any benefit). Everything here is only in the first group. The משנה also records a later change: רבי and his court removed the ban on gentile oil.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban on getting any benefit, such as selling or using
רבי יהודה הנשיא and his court

steps.confusionAlert: "Forbidden" here does not mean you must throw the item away. These foods may not be eaten, but you may still sell them or benefit from them.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And these are items of gentiles that are forbidden
but their prohibition is not a prohibition of benefit:
phrases.notes: So you can't eat them, but you may still sell them or use them in other ways.

phrases.english: Milk that a gentile milked
and a Jew does not see him,
and their bread and their oil.
Rabbi and his court permitted the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם אֲסוּרִין וְאֵין אִיסּוּרָן אִיסּוּר הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the aggadic statements about the תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Milk milked by a גוי without a Jew watching, gentile bread and gentile oil are forbidden to eat but not forbidden for benefit. רבי's court permitted the oil.

steps.title: The list continues with cooked, pickled and fish products
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds boiled and pickled foods usually prepared with wine or vinegar, minced fish, brine without an identifying fish, חילק, a sliver of חלתית and סלקונדית salt. All are forbidden to eat but not forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also boiled and pickled foods that are usually made with wine and vinegar, minced טרית fish, fish brine with no כלבית fish floating in it, חילק, a sliver of חלתית, and סלקונדית salt. All of these are forbidden, but not forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with more gentile foods, then repeats the rule that they are forbidden only for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many of these items carry a hidden risk. They may contain gentile wine or vinegar, or come from a non-kosher fish that cannot be recognized once minced or turned into brine. Because the risk only concerns eating, the ban does not extend to benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher fish whose presence shows the brine is kosher

phrases.english: And boiled foods, and pickled foods
whose usual way is to put wine and vinegar into them,
and minced טרית fish,
and brine that does not have a fish
a כלבית floating in it,
and חילק,
and a sliver of חלתית,
and סלקונדית salt —
these are forbidden,
but their prohibition is not a prohibition of benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין, וְאֵין אִיסּוּרָן אִיסּוּר הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These cooked, pickled and fish products of gentiles are forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.

steps.title: Why should gentile milk be a problem?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the worry about the milk could be. Switching does not work, because kosher milk is white and non-kosher milk is greenish. Mixing does not work either, because one can curdle the milk: kosher milk curdles and non-kosher milk does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we worried about with milk? If the worry is that he swapped in non-kosher milk, kosher milk is white and non-kosher milk is greenish. If the worry is that he mixed some in, just curdle it, since kosher milk curdles and non-kosher milk does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ban on milk a גוי milked. It argues that both possible worries can be easily checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible fears. Swapping is ruled out because the color shows the difference. Mixing is ruled out because a curdling test leaves the non-kosher milk behind. So the ban seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Milk: what should we be worried about?
If it is because of swapping —
phrases.notes: Meaning the גוי might have swapped kosher milk for milk from a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: kosher milk is white, non-kosher milk is greenish!
And if it is because of mixing —
let him curdle it!
As the Master said:
Kosher milk curdles,
non-kosher milk does not curdle.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלָב לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first item in the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on חלב שחלבו גוי ואין ישראל רואהו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible fears, swapping and mixing, can be checked through color or curdling, so no ban should be needed.

steps.title: The ban is for milk used in כמכא, not cheese
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that someone making cheese can rely on curdling. The משנה, however, is talking about someone who wants the milk for כמכא, where no curdling test happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wants the milk for cheese, that is true. But here we are dealing with someone who wants it for כמכא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The curdling test only helps when the milk is made into cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the milk would always be curdled. The answer points out that milk used in a dish like כמכא is never curdled, so mixed-in non-kosher milk could go unnoticed. That is why the ban is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
A milk-based dish, also called כותח

steps.whatToRemember: Gentile milk is forbidden because of the fear of mixed-in non-kosher milk. Curdling would expose that mixture, so this fear matters when the milk is used without curdling, such as in כמכא.

phrases.english: If he wants it for cheese,
indeed, that is so.
Here, what are we dealing with?
Where he wants it for כמכא.
phrases.notes: כמכא is a milk-based dish, so the milk never gets curdled and the test can't be used.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The milk would be curdled, so mixing could always be detected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to milk used for כמכא, where no curdling test happens, so mixing is a real worry.

steps.title: Why not test a little of the milk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the כמכא answer: the person could take a little of the milk, curdle it, and see whether it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him take a little of the milk and curdle it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 17. Even if the milk is for כמכא, why not curdle a small sample as a test?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the worry is only where no curdling happens, as with כמכא. The challenge is that you can always run the curdling test on a small sample. If it works, the whole batch should be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A little bit, a small amount

phrases.english: But let him take a little of it and curdle it!
phrases.notes: He means: test a small sample, since kosher milk curdles and non-kosher milk does not (step 16).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִשְׁקוֹל מִינֵּיהּ קַלִּי וְנֵיקוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the כמכא answer of step 17 by suggesting a sample test.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that milk meant for כמכא has no way to be checked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Curdling a small sample would show whether the milk is kosher, so the worry should go away.

steps.title: The curdling test does not work because kosher milk also leaves whey
steps.stepSummary: Kosher milk also has whey that does not curdle, so leftover liquid in a sample proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since kosher milk also has whey that does not curdle, there is no way to settle the matter by this test.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sample test is useless. Even kosher milk leaves some liquid (whey) after curdling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test needed a clear result: everything curdles means kosher, and leftover liquid means not kosher. Since kosher milk also leaves whey, leftover liquid could be either one. So the test cannot tell us anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher animal (literally, a pure one)
Whey, the watery part of milk that does not curdle
To get to the truth of the matter

phrases.english: Since in a kosher animal's milk too
there is whey that does not curdle,
there is no way to establish the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּבְטָהוֹר נָמֵי אִיכָּא נַסְיוּבֵי דְּלָא קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the proposed test is unreliable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Curdling a sample would show whether the milk is kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whey stays liquid even in kosher milk, so a sample gives no clear answer.

steps.title: Even milk for cheese is a worry because of trapped liquid
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the משנה can apply even to milk meant for cheese, since liquid milk stays in the cracks of the cheese.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: even if he wants it for cheese, there is milk that stays between the cracks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question of step 16. Now the ban covers even someone making cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said cheese makers could rely on curdling. This answer disagrees: some liquid milk stays trapped in the holes of the cheese. That liquid could be non-kosher milk, so curdling does not fully clear the cheese.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not build on step 17. It argues with it, since step 17 said cheese was safe and this says even cheese is a worry.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
you may even say that he wants it for cheese,
there is milk that remains between the crevices.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דְּקָבָעֵי לֵהּ לִגְבִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 16 that replaces the כמכא answer of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer that widens the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cheese is safe because non-kosher milk does not curdle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even cheese may hold drops of uncurdled non-kosher milk in its cracks, so the worry stays.
steps.whatToRemember: The milk of a גוי is forbidden for one of two reasons. Either it is used for כמכא, where nothing is checked, or even cheese can hold uncurdled milk in its cracks.

steps.title: Bread was never permitted by a court
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's word 'bread,' רבי יוחנן says that bread, unlike oil, was not permitted by a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the bread.' רב כהנא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: bread was not permitted by a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the bread of a גוי. רבי יוחנן teaches that no court ever lifted the ban on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that רבי and his court permitted the oil (step 14). רבי יוחנן stresses that bread did not get the same treatment. The ban on bread stayed in place.

phrases.english: And the bread.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 14, which listed the bread of a גוי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Bread was not permitted by a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַפַּת. אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the milk discussion and opens the topic of bread from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No court permitted the bread of a גוי, unlike the oil.

steps.title: Does that mean someone did permit bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי יוחנן's wording that some view must have permitted bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that there is someone who permits it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי יוחנן's words closely. Why say 'bread was not permitted' unless someone thought it was?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stating that something was 'not permitted' suggests there was a real possibility of permitting it. The גמרא asks whether such an opinion actually existed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication; does this imply

phrases.english: Does this imply that there is someone who permits it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא מַאן דְּשָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about what the wording of step 21 implies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there was an opinion that permitted the bread of a גוי.

steps.title: Yes: the story of רבי and the gentile's bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says yes, and brings רב דימי's story about רבי praising a gentile's bread and asking why the Sages forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. When רב דימי came, he said: once רבי went out to the field, and a gentile brought him a large loaf baked in a baker's oven. רבי said: how fine this bread is! Why did the Sages forbid it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story. רבי himself wondered why bread was ever forbidden, which shows there was a move toward permitting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether anyone permitted bread. The story shows רבי asking out loud why the Sages banned such good bread. That is the source of the idea that someone leaned toward permitting it.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A measure of volume; here, a big batch of dough

phrases.english: Yes,
as when Rav Dimi came, he said:
Once Rabbi went out to the field,
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and a gentile brought before him
bread from a large oven, a baking of a se'a.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: כַּמָּה נָאָה פַּת זוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi said: How exquisite is this bread!
What did the Sages see to prohibit it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי questioned the ban on bread, which shows there was a view that leaned toward permitting it.

steps.title: Bread was forbidden because of marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רבי's question with surprise: obviously the Sages forbade bread because of חתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the Sages see?! It was because of marriage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. How could רבי ask why bread was forbidden, when the reason is obvious: to prevent closeness that leads to intermarriage? The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on bread was never about kashrus of the ingredients, so the quality of the bread does not matter. Eating a gentile's bread builds friendship, and that can lead to marriage. That is why the ban stays even for fine bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage ties; here, intermarriage with gentiles

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic reason for the ban on the bread of a גוי. The reason is social, the worry about intermarriage, and not the food itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Bread of a גוי was forbidden משום חתנות, to keep Jews from closeness that leads to intermarriage. That is why no court permitted it, even though the oil was permitted.

phrases.english: What did the Sages see?!
Due to marriage!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רָאוּ חֲכָמִים מִשּׁוּם חַתְנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's question at the end of step 23. The reason for the ban (חתנות) is obvious, so how could he ask? Step 25 answers this.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bread was forbidden to prevent the closeness that leads to intermarriage.

steps.title: רבי was really asking about bread in the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי was not asking why bread is forbidden at all. He was asking why the Sages forbade it even in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי meant: why did the Sages forbid bread even out in the field?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up רבי's question. He knew the reason for the ban (חתנות), and he was only asking why it also applies in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the גמרא was surprised: how could רבי not know the reason for the ban? The answer is that רבי's question was narrower. Out in the field, far from town, the worry about getting close to non-Jews and marrying them seems weaker, so why forbid bread there too?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the גמרא is correcting how we understood something)
What did they see? (What was their reason?)
In the field, out of town

phrases.english: Rather, what did the Sages see
to forbid it in the field?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the bread. Out in the field there is less chance of getting close to non-Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מָה רָאוּ חֲכָמִים לְאוֹסְרָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the surprise of step 24 by narrowing what רבי's question was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the question: רבי's question was limited to the field.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי did not know why bread was forbidden at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי knew the reason (חתנות). He only asked why the ban also applies in the field, where that worry is smaller.

steps.title: People thought רבי permitted bread, but he did not
steps.stepSummary: Because of this story, people mistakenly thought רבי permitted non-Jewish bread. In truth he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people thought רבי permitted the bread. But it is not so. רבי did not permit the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the story back to רבי יוחנן's statement and says that people misread רבי's question as a ruling to permit bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking 'why did they forbid it?' is not the same as permitting it. This explains why רבי יוחנן (step 21) stressed that bread was never permitted by a בית דין: he was correcting a popular mistake.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי only questioned the reason for the ban in the field. He never permitted non-Jewish bread.

phrases.english: The people thought that Rebbi permitted the bread,
but it is not so;
Rebbi did not permit the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּסְבוּרִין הָעָם הִתִּיר רַבִּי הַפַּת, וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the clarified story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Non-Jewish bread was never permitted. People who thought רבי permitted it misunderstood his question.

steps.title: A different version: רבי asked for a baker
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף (or רב שמואל בר יהודה) tells the story differently. רבי saw the students were short of bread and asked if there was no פלטר (baker). People thought he meant a non-Jewish baker, but he meant a Jewish one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, and some say רב שמואל בר יהודה, said: That is not how it happened. Rather, they said: Once רבי went to a place and saw that bread was scarce for the students. רבי said: Is there no baker here? People thought he meant a non-Jewish baker, but he only meant a Jewish baker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of what happened with רבי. In this version too, people misunderstood him as being lenient about non-Jewish bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבי never questioned the ban at all. He just asked for a baker. People took this to mean bread from a non-Jewish professional baker is allowed. The גמרא says that was a misunderstanding: he meant a Jewish baker.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not how the story happened
Bread was scarce, hard to get
A professional baker who sells bread

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling that a baker's bread is allowed. It describes what people wrongly thought, and the גמרא says רבי meant a Jewish baker.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, and some say
Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda, said:
The incident did not happen this way;
rather, they said: Once
Rebbi went to a certain place
and saw that bread was scarce for the students.
Rebbi said: Is there no baker here?
The people thought he meant a gentile baker,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא לֹא אָמַר אֶלָּא פַּלְטֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: but he only meant a Jewish baker.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה, אֶלָּא אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the רבי story, again ending with a popular misunderstanding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's request for a baker meant a Jewish baker. It was not permission to eat a non-Jewish baker's bread.

steps.title: רבי חלבו: only where there is no Jewish baker
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו says that even according to the view that a non-Jewish baker's bread is allowed, this applies only where there is no Jewish baker.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: Even according to the one who says a non-Jewish baker, we only said this where there is no Jewish baker. But where there is a Jewish baker, it is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו puts a limit on the lenient view that allows bread from a non-Jewish baker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose we accept the view that רבי meant a non-Jewish baker. Even then, the leniency only helps when there is no other choice. If a Jewish baker is available, non-Jewish bread stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Where there is not / where there is

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said:
Even according to the one who says a gentile baker,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פַּלְטֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: we said this only where there is no Jewish baker,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּמְקוֹם דְּאִיכָּא פַּלְטֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל — לָא.
phrases.english: but in a place where there is a Jewish baker, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּלְטֵר גּוֹי, לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the lenient reading of the story in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-Jewish baker's bread could be allowed at most only where no Jewish baker is available.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only in the field, not in the city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different limit: even according to the lenient view, a non-Jewish baker's bread is allowed only in the field, not in the city, because of חתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even according to the one who says a non-Jewish baker, that is only in the field. But in the city it is not allowed, because of the worry of marrying non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second limit on the lenient view, based on where the bread is eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חלבו's limit depends on whether a Jewish baker is available. רבי יוחנן's limit depends on place. In the city, where Jews and non-Jews mix closely, the worry about getting close and marrying is strong, so the bread stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two limits on the 'non-Jewish baker' leniency. רבי חלבו: only if there is no Jewish baker. רבי יוחנן: only in the field, never in the city, because of חתנות.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even according to the one who says a gentile baker,
that applies only in the field,
but in the city, no, because of marriage.
phrases.notes: Eating together in town can lead to closeness and marrying non-Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּלְטֵר גּוֹי, הָנֵי מִילֵּי בַּשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different limit than רבי חלבו on the same lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even on the lenient view, a non-Jewish baker's bread is allowed only in the field. In the city it is forbidden because of חתנות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to רבי's question in step 25. The field is exactly where the worry of חתנות is weaker.

steps.title: איבו is criticized for eating non-Jewish bread in the fields
steps.stepSummary: איבו used to eat non-Jewish bread out at the edges of the fields. רבא (or רב נחמן בר יצחק) told people not to talk with him, because he eats the bread of non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: איבו would bite and eat bread at the borders of the fields. רבא, and some say רב נחמן בר יצחק, said to them: Do not talk with איבו, because he eats the bread of non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how seriously the Sages took the ban on non-Jewish bread, even out in the fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איבו ate this bread in the field, the very place where some might be lenient. Even so, רבא told people to keep away from him, which shows the ban was treated as binding.

phrases.english: Aivu would bite
and eat bread at the borders of the fields.
Rava said to them,
and some say Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
Do not speak with Aivu,
because he eats the bread of Arameans.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְבוּ הֲוָה מְנַכֵּית וְאָכֵיל פַּת אַבֵּי מִצְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story showing that the ban on non-Jewish bread was enforced even in the field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who eats non-Jewish bread, even out in the fields, deserves to be kept at a distance.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה: their oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item from the משנה's list: the oil of non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And their oil."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is done with bread and turns to the next item in the משנה, the oil of non-Jews. This short quote opens a new topic and sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a pointer back to the משנה, not a new ruling. It tells us that the next lines are about oil, not bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil, here the oil of non-Jews

phrases.english: And their oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁלָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of non-Jewish bread to the next item in the משנה, oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the discussion of non-Jewish oil from the משנה.

steps.title: רב says דניאל decreed against the oil
steps.stepSummary: רב says that דניאל made the decree banning non-Jewish oil. The גמרא then starts to give שמואל's different view.
steps.simpleTranslation: About oil: רב said that דניאל made a decree against it. And שמואל said: (his words continue on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about where the ban on non-Jewish oil came from. רב says דניאל made the decree, and the גמרא is now setting up שמואל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question here is about the source of the ban, not about whether oil was ever forbidden. רב traces it all the way back to דניאל. The words "ושמואל אמר" show that שמואל is about to give a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: דניאל, the prophet from ספר דניאל
"רב says ... and שמואל says", the standard opening for a מחלוקת between them

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's view is not finished here. The sentence stops at "ושמואל אמר", and his opinion comes right after.

phrases.english: Oil: Rav says:
Daniel decreed against it,
and Shmuel says:
phrases.notes: שמואל's actual words come at the top of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמֶן, רַב אָמַר: דָּנִיאֵל גָּזַר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the discussion of the oil just quoted from the משנה with a מחלוקת about who first banned it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the ban on non-Jewish oil goes back to a decree of דניאל. שמואל's view follows.
